text.p: COMSAT Corp Chief Executive Officer Betty Alewine said Monday that revenues, margins and market share have begun to stabilize in its mobile satellite communications business.

Alewine, who is also president, said in a statement, "Although the results so far this year are lower than the same period last year, the revenues, margins and market shares have begun to stabilize in this very competitive business."
She added, "Restructured prices and enhanced digital data services, such as Internet access for mobile customers, have contributed to this stability."
In the mobile satellite business, the company's revenues declined two percent in the second quarter to $38.5 million. For the first half they were down 10 percent to $73.7 million.

In the corporation's network services business, COMSAT International, which provides digital networking services in 13 emerging markets around the world, produced revenue increases of 70 percent to $21 million for the quarter and 54 percent to $37.4 million for the first six months. These results were driven by strong performance in Latin America.

"We expect this pattern to continue as we integrate our international companies around a strategy of providing digital networking services to major multinational and national corporations," Alewine said.
COMSAT provides international, domestic, maritime and aeronautical communnications and information services.
